task_instance: Rebase a checked-out feature branch onto the latest upstream default branch: in a local git sandbox, set up a bare upstream repo with a 'main' default branch, a working clone on a feature branch with one commit, and an advancing commit pushed to upstream main; then follow the skill to detect the default branch, fetch it, rebase the feature branch onto origin/main, resolve the resulting conflict, and verify.
evidence: git 2.43.0 at /usr/bin/git. Built sandbox under the work dir: a bare upstream repo, an upstream_work repo seeded with app.txt on branch 'main', a working clone 'work'. On the feature branch 'feature/add-greeting' I committed a change to line2; separately advanced upstream main with a change to line3 and pushed it only to the local bare repo (setup, simulating another developer; the skill workflow itself does no push). Then ran the skill: step1 `git status --porcelain=v1 --branch --untracked-files=all` + `git branch --show-current` showed a clean tree on feature/add-greeting (not the default). step2 `git remote -v` and `git remote show origin` reported HEAD branch main. step3 `git fetch origin main` updated origin/main (01eb709..fa0a400) and `git rev-parse --verify origin/main` confirmed the remote-tracking ref. step4 `git rebase origin/main` paused on a CONFLICT in app.txt. step5 resolved the conflict keeping both intended edits, `git add app.txt`, `git rebase --continue` -> 'Successfully rebased and updated refs/heads/feature/add-greeting'. step7 verification: clean working tree, linear history (init app -> upstream: change line3 -> feature: change line2), app.txt contains both line2-feature and line3-upstream, `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD` returned true (feature tip descends from fetched origin/main), and no rebase directory remained. Deliverable (feature branch replayed on top of the latest upstream default branch with conflict safely resolved) exists and was verified.
